papers.title: Infrared Thermographic Evaluation of Temperature Modifications Induced during Implant Site Preparation with Steel vs. Zirconia Implant Drill.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The heat produced during implant site osteotomy can potentially interfere with and influence the osseointegration process of a dental implant. The objective of this in vitro investigation was to measure the temperature changes during simulated osteotomies in bovine rib bone. The measurements were made at the apical area of the osteotomies with steel implant drills compared to zirconia implant drills. METHODS: Steel cylindrical drills (2 mm) and zirconia cylindrical drills (2 mm) were evaluated in vitro using bovine rib bone for a total of five groups based on the number of osteotomies performed with each drill: 10, 20, 40, 90, or 120 osteotomies. Bone and apical drill temperatures were measured by means of infrared thermography. The drilling time for each osteotomy was measured for each preparation. RESULTS: Statistically significant differences were found in the temperature measurements in the bone and apical portion of the drills between the study groups (p < 0.05). A statistically significant difference was observed for drilling time preparation between steel cylindrical drill (2 mm) and zirconia cylindrical drills (2 mm) (p < 0.01). CONCLUSIONS: The drill material has an impact on the temperature changes that occur at its apical portion during bone preparation for implant placement.

llm.relevance_to_user: 本文与用户研究方向无关，未涉及AM生物医用材料的制造、力学性能或骨整合。
llm.why_not_core: No LPBF fabrication, no porous structure, no mechanical testing (static or fatigue), no surface roughness or osseointegration related to AM implants.

summary_zh.motivation: 测量不同材料钻头制备骨床时的温度变化。
summary_zh.method: 用钢钻和氧化锆钻在牛肋骨上模拟种植窝制备，红外热成像测温。
summary_zh.result: 钻头材料显著影响骨和钻尖的温度及钻孔时间。
summary_zh.validation: 体外牛骨实验，统计学比较组间差异。

summary_en.motivation: To evaluate the temperature rise during implant site osteotomy using different drill materials.
summary_en.method: Steel and zirconia cylindrical drills were used to perform osteotomies in bovine rib bone, and temperatures were measured via infrared thermography.
summary_en.result: Significant differences in bone and drill tip temperatures were observed between steel and zirconia drills, with zirconia drills causing higher temperatures.
summary_en.validation: In vitro experiment with bovine rib bone and statistical comparisons among groups.
